remoteDiagnostics.noSession: no session ; tRPC will be called as anon, every authed query returns empty

hints.apiUnreachable: Connection failed before the server responded. Likely : Windows Firewall blocks inbound 4000 ; api isn't on 0.0.0.0 ; not on the same LAN ; the resolved URL above is still loopback.
hints.apiRejected: API replied but rejected. Check api stderr for a CORS warning.
hints.supabaseUnreachable: Supabase Docker binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. On Windows, run `tools/dev-lan-setup.ps1` to add a portproxy + firewall rule.
hints.getSessionThrew: Browser-side Supabase client threw on getSession() ; check the browser console.
hints.staleCookie: You signed in before the storage-key pin landed. The browser has a cookie under a stale name (the client now looks for "{key}"). Use the button below to clear stale cookies + re-sign-in.
hints.cookiesUnreadable: Auth cookies present but the browser-side Supabase client can't read them. Open the cookies panel in DevTools and confirm the cookie name matches the pinned storage key.
hints.noCookies: No `sb-*` cookies on this device. Did you actually sign in *from this device* (not your laptop) ? Cookies don't sync across devices.
hints.meRejected: Browser has a session + token but the api rejected the request. Most often : api can't validate the JWT against Supabase ; or CORS blocked the Authorization header.
hints.meThrew: Authed tRPC fetch failed. Check api stderr for a stack trace.

github.title: GitHub
github.subtitle: Connect a repository so GitHub events can trigger automations, and use GitHub nodes to read + write.
github.noPermission: You don't have permission to manage the GitHub connection.
github.webhookHint: Point a repository's (or org's) GitHub webhook here so its events reach your automations.
github.secretOnce: Copy this secret now — it won't be shown again.
github.step1: In your repository: Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook.
github.step2: Set the Payload URL to the Webhook URL above, Content type to application/json, and the Secret to the generated secret.
github.step3: Choose the events to send (issues, issue comments, pull requests, pushes, releases).
github.step4: Add a secret named for your GitHub token (a fine-grained PAT) under Admin → Secrets, then reference it in the token field of your GitHub automation nodes.

telegram.title: Telegram
telegram.subtitle: Connect a Telegram bot so its messages can trigger automations, and use Telegram nodes to send messages back.
telegram.noPermission: You don't have permission to manage the Telegram connection.
telegram.connectHint: Paste your bot token to connect. We'll register the webhook with Telegram so its messages reach your automations.
telegram.connectedHint: Telegram is connected. Its messages reach your automations at the webhook URL below.
telegram.step1: In Telegram, message @BotFather and send /newbot to create a bot (or /token for an existing one).
telegram.step2: Copy the HTTP API token BotFather gives you and paste it above, then Connect.
telegram.step3: Requires a public HTTPS URL Telegram can reach — connecting from localhost won't work (Telegram rejects non-public webhooks).
telegram.step4: Add your bot to a group or start a chat with it, then use the Telegram trigger events + nodes in your automations.

twitter.title: X (Twitter)
twitter.subtitle: Connect an X account so automations can post, reply, and delete tweets. Write-only — X has no trigger events.
twitter.noPermission: You don't have permission to manage the X connection.
twitter.connectHint: Paste your app's OAuth 1.0a credentials from the X developer portal. They're stored write-only and used to sign requests.
twitter.connectedHint: X is connected. Your automations can post with the X action nodes.
twitter.setupHeading: Set up in the X developer portal
twitter.step1: At developer.x.com, create a Project + App (a paid tier is required for most access; the free tier allows posting).
twitter.step2: In the app's User authentication settings, enable OAuth 1.0a with Read and write permissions.
twitter.step3: Under Keys and tokens, copy the API key/secret and generate an Access token/secret for your account.
twitter.step4: Paste all four above and Connect. The credentials are stored encrypted and never shown again.

discord.title: Discord
discord.subtitle: Post messages to Discord from your automations. Write-only — Discord has no trigger events.
discord.writeOnly: Discord is write-only: automation nodes send messages using either a bot token or a channel webhook URL. There's no connection to set up here.
discord.secrets: Add your bot token or a channel webhook URL as a secret under Admin → Secrets, then reference it in the token / webhook field of a Discord automation node.
discord.step1: For a bot: create an app at discord.com/developers, add a bot, copy its token, and invite the bot to your server with the Send Messages permission.
discord.step2: For a webhook (no bot): in a channel, Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook, then copy its URL.
discord.step3: Store the token or webhook URL as a secret, then add a Discord node in an automation and select it.
